notes:
One genus under two spellings. "Echino-encrinus" heads the English
description (p. 504), the character table (p. 494) and the species
headings "Echino-encrinus baccatus, Forbes" and "E. armatus"
(pp. 506–507). "Echino-encrinites" is used when citing "his genus"
of Von Meyer (p. 504), in the Latin summary heading with "1. E.
armatus" and "2. E. baccatus" (pp. 509–510), in the general prose
("most Echino-encrinites", p. 485) and in the chart (p. 526).
subject: echino-encrinus

text:
Body hemisphæric, slightly depressed above, with a concave base,
the margins of which are rounded. The mouth appears to have been
in the centre of the summit, and from it radiate deep canals or
grooves, five in number, regularly bordered by close parallel ridges
and sulcations.  These canals ( in which the arms are lodged) are
each and all curved
